home: This is envoy. It helps residents find public services and take the next step when something is wrong.
Envoy connects residents to public sources, services, and a report inbox in one place.
Anyone can begin as a guest. The assistant, service finder, and feedback entry point are visible without an account.
sources: A useful civic journey starts with a source people can trust.
Here, envoy brings together individual government job postings, public consultations, and nearby service locations.
Each job posting keeps its publisher, location, closing date, and original link. Residents can compare openings without losing the source.
The consultation view shows who is asking for input and when the window closes, then sends residents to the publisher to respond.
Nearby services show locations and source links. Confirm current hours with the agency before visiting.
The SwiftUI companion also shows nearby services on an iPhone simulator.
Physical-device and production API checks remain ahead for the native app.
agent: A resident can describe a civic issue in ordinary language, without choosing a form first.
A resident asks how to report a damaged bench at Nathan Phillips Square in Toronto.
Workers AI replies with a feedback preview, and envoy shows a pending approval card with editable words.
The card names envoy's review team as the destination and says the City of Toronto does not receive the report.
The resident can edit or decline. This report remains unsubmitted.
feedback: Guests can share a concern in their own words and see where their report will go.
The form moves to a review screen and states that no government office receives it.
Before sending, envoy shows the destination and asks for an explicit acknowledgement.
Envoy issues a private receipt after submission. The review screen shown here remains unsubmitted.
For an emergency, residents must use emergency services. This inbox is not monitored for urgent response.
tiger: After a resident confirms submission to Envoy, D1 stores the case as the source of truth.
An outbox sends privacy-safe event metadata to Tiger for time-series analysis. It does not send the resident's message body.
The September twenty-sixth Tiger snapshot shows how feedback events were delivered.
It showed four delivered feedback events and four events in the daily aggregate. Two were submitted and classified events for an earlier Envoy report.
Counts can change as new reports arrive. The displayed timestamp keeps this result in context.
staff: A staff workspace needs stronger evidence than a sign-in screen.
Auth0 hosted sign-in and an Envoy organization are configured, but a live staff role token and scoped case action have not yet passed acceptance.
The Worker checks Auth0 grants and matching organization membership before a staff action.
A staff reply becomes available only after those checks pass with a real token.
The team is verifying a permitted case action and a denied unauthorized action before showing staff work live.
closing: envoy combines official source handoffs, a guest assistant, and reviewable resident feedback.
Real places and source links appear alongside Envoy's own report inbox. No government office receives these reports.
The next milestone is a participating organization and verified staff access.
